questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Supreme Court's judgment in Harish Rana v. Union of India (March 2026):
1. It was the first application of the passive-euthanasia framework laid down in the Aruna Shanbaug case (2011).
2. The Court permitted withdrawal of life-sustaining treatment, including clinically assisted nutrition through a PEG tube, for a man in a permanent vegetative state for over 13 years.
3. The bench comprised Justices J.B. Pardiwala and K.V. Viswanathan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is wrong: the framework applied was the one laid down in Common Cause v. Union of India (2018), which recognised passive euthanasia and advance directives as part of the right to die with dignity under Article 21. Aruna Shanbaug (2011) had earlier allowed passive euthanasia only in principle, under court supervision. Statements 2 and 3 correctly state the 11 March 2026 ruling.
questions.s: Supreme Court Observer / Drishti IAS, 11 Mar 2026
questions.h: Shanbaug 2011 opened the door; Common Cause 2018 built the framework; Harish Rana 2026 used it

questions.q: In Rachana Gangu v. Union of India (10 March 2026), the Supreme Court directed the Union Government to:
o: pay compensation to the families of those who died after the Court found that specific deaths were caused by Covid-19 vaccines
enact a law making Covid-19 vaccination compulsory for all adults
frame a no-fault compensation policy for serious adverse events or deaths following Covid-19 vaccination, without attributing any death to the vaccines
replace the existing AEFI committees with a statutory tribunal that adjudicates individual vaccine-injury claims
questions.e: The Court did not hold that any death was caused by the vaccines; it asked the Centre to frame a no-fault scheme, so compensation does not depend on proving causation or fault. The Centre's plea that families should chase individual civil or consumer remedies was rejected, with the Court relying on Article 21. A statute making vaccination compulsory would run against the Puliyel (2022) position that no one can be forcibly vaccinated.

questions.q:
Statement-I: In Union of India v. Rohith Nathan (March 2026), the Supreme Court held that parental salary income alone cannot decide whether a candidate belongs to the OBC creamy layer.
Statement-II: Creamy-layer status for OBCs is primarily status-based, depending on the category of the post held by the parent.
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The Bench of Justices P.S. Narasimha and R. Mahadevan treated creamy-layer exclusion as turning mainly on the parent's status (the category of post held), so salary income cannot by itself push a candidate into the creamy layer. Statement-II is the reasoning behind Statement-I. The Court also held that a 2004 DoPT clarification cannot override the 1993 Office Memorandum issued after Indra Sawhney.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Hamsaanandini Nanduri v. Union of India (judgment dated 17 March 2026):
1. The Supreme Court struck down the age limit in Section 60(4) of the Code on Social Security, 2020.
2. Any woman legally adopting a child is entitled to 12 weeks of maternity leave irrespective of the child's age.
3. The struck-down provision formed part of the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The impugned age ceiling sat in the Code on Social Security, 2020, which has replaced the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961, so statement 3 wrongly places it in the old Act. By removing the cap, the Court extended the 12-week benefit to every legally adopting woman regardless of the child's age. The Court also urged the Union to consider statutory paternity leave.
questions.h: Adoptive mother: 12 weeks, any age of child

questions.q:
With reference to Chinthada Anand v. State of Andhra Pradesh (24 March 2026), consider the following statements:
1. The Supreme Court upheld Paragraph 3 of the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950.
2. Only persons professing Hinduism, Sikhism or Buddhism can be treated as Scheduled Castes.
3. Conversion to any other religion ends Scheduled Caste status.
4. The 1950 Order was issued by Parliament by law under Article 341.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Court upheld Paragraph 3, so SC status is confined to Hindus, Sikhs and Buddhists, and a convert to another religion loses it. Statement 4 is wrong: the Order was issued by the President under Article 341(1); Parliament can only modify the list by law under Article 341(2). Sikhs were added in 1956 and Buddhists in 1990 through such amendments.
questions.s: Drishti IAS / PRS / Supreme Court Observer, 24 Mar 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026:
1. It was introduced in the Lok Sabha on 25 March 2026.
2. On cancellation, surrender or cessation of an FCRA registration, foreign contributions and assets created from them vest permanently and immediately in the Central Government.
3. The parent Act, the FCRA, 2010, is administered by the Ministry of Home Affairs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Bill provides that such contributions and assets vest only provisionally in a Designated Authority, and become permanent if no fresh or renewed registration is obtained within the prescribed period; the vesting is therefore neither immediate-permanent nor in the Central Government directly. Statements 1 and 3 are correct, as the MHA administers the FCRA, 2010.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 is correct?
o: It was introduced in the Rajya Sabha on 23 March 2026 and referred to the Departmentally Related Standing Committee on Finance
It was passed by the Lok Sabha on 23 March 2026 and referred to a Select Committee of the Rajya Sabha
It was introduced in the Lok Sabha on 23 March 2026 and withdrawn after a Select Committee presented its report
It was introduced in the Lok Sabha on 23 March 2026 and referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee
questions.e: The Bill was introduced on 23 March 2026 and sent to a Joint Parliamentary Committee, an ad hoc body with members from both Houses. It was therefore not passed in that session. It is distinct from the Jan Vishwas Bill, which was examined by a Select Committee of the Lok Sabha.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Bill (2026) : Parliamentary action in March 2026
1. Finance Bill, 2026 : Passed by the Lok Sabha on 25 March by voice vote
2. Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Bill : Passed by Parliament on 25 March when the Rajya Sabha approved it
3. Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill : Passed by both Houses on 25 March
4. Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Bill, 2025 : Passed by the Lok Sabha on 17 March
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct; the Transgender Bill cleared the Lok Sabha by voice vote on 24 March and the Rajya Sabha on 25 March. The FCRA Amendment Bill was only introduced on 25 March, and the 2025 Jan Vishwas Bill was withdrawn on 17 March after the Select Committee reported, to be replaced by a fresh 2026 Bill.
questions.s: Drishti IAS / PRS / AIR News, 17-25 Mar 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Finance Bill, 2026:
1. The Lok Sabha passed it on 25 March 2026 by voice vote after incorporating 32 government amendments.
2. The amendments cut tax collected at source (TCS) on overseas tour packages to 2% from 20%.
3. The amendments cut TCS on overseas tour packages to 5% from 20%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statements 2 and 3 contradict each other, and the reduction was to 2%, not 5%. The Finance Bill was one of the nine Bills passed in the 2026 Budget Session, and the new Income Tax Act, 2025 takes effect from 1 April 2026.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Lok Sabha passing the Demands for Grants for 2026-27 by the guillotine:
1. Under the guillotine, all remaining demands are put to vote at a fixed time without detailed discussion.
2. The Rajya Sabha votes on the Demands for Grants and can reject them.
3. Demands for Grants are presented to Parliament under Article 113 of the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The guillotine closes debate at a fixed hour and puts all pending demands to vote together, which is how most demands are passed. Only the Lok Sabha votes on Demands for Grants (the 'power of the purse'); the Rajya Sabha may merely discuss and make recommendations, so statement 2 is wrong. Under Article 113, expenditure estimates not charged on the Consolidated Fund go to the Lok Sabha as Demands for Grants.
questions.h: Guillotine = the clock chops the debate

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the biennial Rajya Sabha elections of 16 March 2026:
1. Seats were filled across 37 vacancies in 10 states.
2. The Rajya Sabha has 245 members, of whom 12 are nominated by the President.
3. All members of the Rajya Sabha retire together every six years.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Elections were held for 37 seats across 10 states, with 26 candidates returned unopposed. The Rajya Sabha is a permanent House: one-third of its members retire every second year, so statement 3 is wrong. Its strength is 233 elected by state/UT legislatures plus 12 nominated, a total of 245.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Election Commission's announcement of 15 March 2026 for the assembly elections:
1. Assam, Kerala and Puducherry vote on 9 April.
2. Tamil Nadu votes in a single phase on 9 April along with Kerala.
3. West Bengal votes in two phases, on 23 and 29 April.
4. Counting of votes for all the states is on 24 April.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Assam, Kerala and Puducherry vote on 9 April, Tamil Nadu on 23 April, and West Bengal on 23 and 29 April, so statements 1 and 3 are right. Counting for all five is on 4 May 2026, not 24 April. The Model Code of Conduct took effect on announcement under the Election Commission's Article 324 powers.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Governor and Lieutenant Governor changes of 5 March 2026:
1. R.N. Ravi was moved from Tamil Nadu to West Bengal.
2. Former diplomat Taranjit Singh Sandhu was appointed Lieutenant Governor of Delhi.
3. Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar, Governor of Kerala, was permanently transferred to Tamil Nadu in place of R.N. Ravi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Ravi went to West Bengal and Sandhu became Delhi's Lieutenant Governor, whose special powers flow from Article 239AA. Arlekar, the Kerala Governor, was only given additional charge of Tamil Nadu, not transferred, so statement 3 is wrong. Governors are appointed by the President under Article 155.

questions.q: The Union Cabinet on 25 March 2026 approved continuation of the Immigration, Visa, Foreigners Registration & Tracking (IVFRT) Scheme. Which one of the following correctly describes the decision?
o: It will run from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031 with an outlay of Rs 1,800 crore under the Ministry of Home Affairs
It will run from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031 with an outlay of Rs 1,800 crore under the Ministry of External Affairs
It will run from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2029 with an outlay of Rs 1,800 crore under the Ministry of Home Affairs
It will run from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031 with an outlay of Rs 18,000 crore under the Ministry of Home Affairs
questions.e: IVFRT is a Ministry of Home Affairs scheme, first approved in 2010, and its Bureau of Immigration modernises immigration check posts. The 2026 approval covers five years and Rs 1,800 crore, and adds features such as iris scanning, AI/ML tools and self-service kiosks. It is not a Ministry of External Affairs scheme, which handles passports and visas abroad.

questions.q:
Statement-I: In March 2026 a nine-judge Constitution Bench led by CJI Surya Kant reserved judgment on whether Bangalore Water Supply v. A. Rajappa (1978) correctly defined 'industry' under Section 2(j) of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947.
Statement-II: The Rajappa 'triple test' gave 'industry' a wide meaning that includes many service and charitable establishments.
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Rajappa's triple test brought hospitals, universities and charities within 'industry', and the nine-judge Bench is reconsidering whether that breadth is correct. Statement-II is the reason the case is being revisited, so it explains Statement-I. A larger Bench is needed because the Court is reconsidering an earlier Constitution Bench precedent.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Union's appeal against the Bombay High Court judgment on the government fact-check unit (Supreme Court, 10 March 2026):
1. The High Court had struck down the fact-check unit set up under the 2023 amendment to the IT Rules.
2. The Supreme Court refused to stay the High Court judgment and directed that a three-judge bench hear the matter.
3. The High Court had upheld the unit as a reasonable restriction under Article 19(2).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Bombay High Court held the unit unconstitutional, so statement 3 is the reverse of what happened. The Supreme Court issued notice, declined to stay the ruling and referred the matter to a three-judge bench. The core question is whether the unit is a valid restriction on free speech under Article 19(2).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of West Bengal's electoral rolls:
1. The Supreme Court directed on 10 March 2026 that all deleted names be restored automatically without any appeal.
2. On 24 March the Court asked parties to approach the Chief Justice of the Calcutta High Court to supervise the process.
3. The revision is carried out by the Election Commission of India ahead of the 2026 assembly election.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Court directed an appellate mechanism for persons whose names were deleted, not automatic restoration, so statement 1 is wrong. The Court then routed supervision through the Chief Justice of the Calcutta High Court. Preparation and revision of electoral rolls is the Election Commission's function under Article 324.

questions.q:
Match the Parliamentary Standing Committee (chair) in List-I with its March 2026 report in List-II:
List-I
A. Empowerment of Women (Dr D. Purandeswari)
B. Communications and IT (Dr Nishikant Dubey)
C. Agriculture (Charanjit Singh Channi)
D. Health and Family Welfare (Prof. Ram Gopal Yadav)
List-II
1. Report No. 27 on Artificial Intelligence
2. 171st report on AIIMS, New Delhi
3. Report on cyber crimes and cyber safety of women
4. Report recommending wider PM-AASHA procurement and a new Seeds Bill
questions.e: The Women's Empowerment panel dealt with cyber safety (citing a 239% rise in cybercrimes against women in 2017-22), the IT panel with AI regulation, the Agriculture panel with PM-AASHA and the Seeds Act, 1966, and the Health panel with AIIMS Delhi. Departmentally related standing committees examine demands and subjects of their ministries.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Standing Committees' reports presented in March 2026:
1. The Standing Committee on Agriculture recommended expanding PM-AASHA procurement of oilseeds and pulses from 25% to 50% of production.
2. The same committee suggested replacing the Seeds Act, 1966 with a new Seeds Bill.
3. The Standing Committee on Communications and IT recommended that the government explore comprehensive AI legislation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Agriculture committee (chair Charanjit Singh Channi) recommended raising PM-AASHA procurement from 25% to 100% of production, not 50%. It also favoured replacing the Seeds Act, 1966. The IT committee's Report No. 27 asked the government to explore comprehensive AI legislation and age restrictions on certain platforms.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Census 2027 mascots and tools unveiled on 5 March 2026:
1. The mascot Pragati represents men and Vikas represents women.
2. Four digital tools developed with C-DAC were soft-launched, including a Self-Enumeration portal.
3. The Census is conducted under the Census Act, 1948.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Union Home Minister Amit Shah unveiled Pragati for women and Vikas for men, so statement 1 reverses them. The four C-DAC tools include the House Listing Block Creator, the HLO mobile app, the Self-Enumeration portal and the Census Management and Monitoring System. The Census is a Union subject conducted by the Registrar General under the Census Act, 1948.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Garo Hills Autonomous District Council (Meghalaya):
1. Its polls, earlier set for 10 April 2026, were postponed after unrest over a notification requiring candidates to hold a Scheduled Tribe certificate.
2. The Council's term was extended by six months.
3. Autonomous District Councils are provided for under Article 244(1) of the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both the postponement and the six-month extension of the Council's term are reported facts. Autonomous District Councils exist under the Sixth Schedule, linked to Article 244(2); Article 244(1) concerns the Fifth Schedule (Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes in other states), so statement 3 is wrong. Meghalaya has three ADCs: Garo Hills, Khasi Hills and Jaintia Hills.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about decisions of the Union Cabinet on 10 March 2026:
1. It approved declaring Madurai airport in Tamil Nadu an international airport.
2. It extended the Jal Jeevan Mission to December 2030.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Cabinet approved international status for Madurai airport. It extended the Jal Jeevan Mission (Ministry of Jal Shakti) to December 2028, not 2030. The same meeting approved a Rs 3,839.42 crore four-lane NH-752D corridor in Madhya Pradesh.

questions.q: Which one of the following correctly describes the fate of the Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Bill, 2025 in March 2026?
o: It was withdrawn from the Lok Sabha on 17 March after a Joint Parliamentary Committee chaired by Tejasvi Surya reported, and replaced by a 2026 Bill amending 80 central Acts
It was withdrawn from the Lok Sabha on 17 March after the Select Committee chaired by Tejasvi Surya reported, and replaced by a 2026 Bill amending 80 central Acts
It was withdrawn from the Lok Sabha on 17 March after the Select Committee chaired by Tejasvi Surya reported, and replaced by a 2026 Bill amending 17 central Acts
It was passed by the Lok Sabha on 17 March after the Select Committee chaired by Tejasvi Surya recommended no changes
questions.e: The Select Committee presented its report on 13 March, after which the 2025 Bill (which amended 17 Acts) was withdrawn and a new 2026 Bill amending 80 Acts was brought. A Select Committee is appointed by one House, unlike a Joint Parliamentary Committee. The 2026 Bill went on to pass in early April.

questions.q:
Match the March 2026 Supreme Court case in List-I with its subject in List-II:
List-I
A. Harish Rana v. Union of India
B. Rachana Gangu v. Union of India
C. Hamsaanandini Nanduri v. Union of India
D. Union of India v. Rohith Nathan
List-II
1. Parental status and OBC creamy layer
2. Maternity leave for adoptive mothers
3. Withdrawal of life-sustaining treatment
4. No-fault compensation after Covid-19 vaccination
questions.e: Harish Rana (11 March) applied the passive-euthanasia framework, Rachana Gangu (10 March) concerned a no-fault compensation policy, Hamsaanandini Nanduri (17 March) struck down the age limit on adoptive-mother maternity leave, and Rohith Nathan (11-12 March) held creamy-layer status is primarily status-based.
questions.s: Supreme Court Observer / Drishti IAS, Mar 2026

questions.q: In Prabhu Kumar v. State of Himachal Pradesh (2026), the Supreme Court held that:
o: a State may fix a 60% upper disability ceiling for Assistant District Attorneys because public prosecution is a sensitive post
persons with disabilities above 40% cannot claim reservation in State judicial services under the RPwD Act, 2016
the RPwD Act, 2016 prescribes a 60% benchmark disability that the State may not lower
a State cannot fix an arbitrary 60% upper disability ceiling for appointment as Assistant District Attorney when the RPwD Act, 2016 prescribes only a 40% benchmark disability
questions.e: The RPwD Act, 2016 defines a person with benchmark disability as one with at least 40% disability. The Court said suitability must rest on the functional requirements of the post, not a percentage bracket, and found the cap violated Articles 14 and 16. The Himachal Pradesh High Court had upheld the cap, so it was reversed.
